standard_prerequisites.name: A relatively very ample sheaf makes the morphism separated, cited from the same chapter, together with locality of separatedness on the base
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives separatedness needed for the pushforward of the sheaf to be quasi-coherent and for the formulation of the fourth condition.

standard_prerequisites.name: Pushforward along a quasi-compact separated morphism preserves quasi-coherence, cited from the schemes chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the pushforward of the invertible sheaf a quasi-coherent module so that its projective bundle and the associated morphism make sense.

standard_prerequisites.name: The description of a morphism into a projective bundle by a surjection from a pullback of a module, and the adjunction with a map into the pushforward, cited from the constructions chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts the local immersions into projective bundles into the surjectivity statement of the fourth condition.

standard_prerequisites.name: The open subscheme of morphisms of relative Proj's induced by a map of modules, and the closed immersion of relative Proj's induced by a surjection from a symmetric algebra generated in degree one
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the open U_j through which the associated morphism factors, and the final implication from the third condition to the first.

core_obligations: Dispose of the easy implications: the first implies the second by restriction to the members of a cover, and the fourth implies the first, where the quasi-separation hypothesis is what makes the pushforward quasi-coherent (proof lines 9165-9172).

From the second to the fourth condition: the morphism is separated by locality on the base, and on each member of the cover the hypothesis provides a module and an immersion into its projective bundle realizing the invertible sheaf as the pullback of the twisting sheaf; the corresponding surjection is adjoint to a map from the module into the pushforward, whose composition with the canonical map from the pullback of the pushforward is surjective, which gives surjectivity of the canonical map globally (proof lines 9174-9196).

Immersiveness in the fourth condition: the map of modules over each member of the cover induces a morphism from an open subscheme of the projective bundle of the pushforward into the projective bundle of that module, compatibility of the two maps shows that the associated morphism lands in that open subscheme and factors through the immersion already available, so the associated morphism is an immersion (proof lines 9196-9217).

Close the cycle: the fourth condition clearly implies the third, and conversely, given a graded algebra generated in degree one with a compatible surjective map from the pullback of its degree one part, the canonical map from its symmetric algebra onto it is surjective by hypothesis, hence induces a closed immersion of the corresponding relative Proj's pulling back the twisting sheaf to the twisting sheaf, which recovers the first condition (proof lines 9219-9237).
proof_roadmap: Note the trivial implications and reduce the main work to passing from the local condition to the global one, where separatedness and adjunction produce the surjectivity of the canonical map (proof lines 9165-9196).

Factor the associated morphism through an open subscheme of the projective bundle to get immersiveness, then close the cycle by exhibiting a relative Proj as a closed subscheme of a projective bundle (proof lines 9196-9237).
difficulty_reason: The lemma collects four equivalent formulations of relative very ampleness for an invertible sheaf on a quasi-compact morphism: the definition, its being local on the base, an explicit graded algebra presentation with an immersion into a relative Proj, and the classical condition on the canonical map from the pullback of the pushforward being surjective with the associated morphism an immersion (statement lines 9145-9169). The counted proof has real content in two places: the passage from the local condition to the global one, where separatedness and adjunction produce surjectivity of the canonical map, and the verification that the associated morphism is an immersion by factoring it through an open subscheme of the projective bundle of the pushforward; the cycle is then closed by presenting a relative Proj as a closed subscheme of a projective bundle (proof lines 9165-9237). It is H2: the implications are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard projective bundle and relative Proj statements.
